insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies by plan; e.g., Optima Secure: 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs as per Annexure C)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be At Actuals unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: Room rent is covered at actual cost without any predefined limit unless the schedule states otherwise. This means you can choose any room type without worrying about a fixed cap.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Extra insurer-provided Sum Insured becomes available after the base Sum Insured is used up. This helps cover large claims beyond your base limit.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.explanation: Sum Insured is replenished and can be used for the same illness again within the policy year. This provides extra coverage without waiting for renewal.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.explanation: Sum Insured increases on renewal even if you have made claims, unlike typical bonuses that reset. This rewards claim-free years without penalty.

great.name: SI Utilization
great.quote: The sequence of utilization of Sum Insured in this Policy will be as follows... b. Base Sum Insured. c. Cumulative Bonus/Plus Benefit d. Secure Benefit e. Automatic Restore Benefit
great.reference: Section D 	6 1.19 Utilization of Sum Insured (Page 39)
great.explanation: Clear rules define how different Sum Insured buffers are used during claims. This reduces confusion and ensures proper claim settlement.

great.name: PED Waiting
great.quote: Modification of PED waiting period from 36 months... to 24 months (2 years)... to 12 months (1 year)
great.reference: Section B.2.12 	6 PED waiting period modification (Page 25)
great.explanation: You can opt for a reduced pre-existing disease waiting period as low as 12 months. This means earlier coverage for pre-existing conditions if chosen.

great.name: Air Ambulance
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred... towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care...
great.explanation: Air ambulance transport is covered if this optional benefit is in force. This provides critical emergency transport support.

good.name: PED Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months from policy start. This is a standard waiting period in the market.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section C.1(b)(i) 	6 Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period (Page 28-29)
good.explanation: Specific illnesses have a 24-month waiting period before coverage begins. This is typical for many health policies.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days except accidents. This is a common initial waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps with costs leading up to hospital admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 180 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs after hospital stay.

good.name: Optional Cover
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non-Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B to this Policy incurred in relation to a claim admissible under Section B -1 (Base Coverage)...
good.explanation: You can opt for a cover that reimburses certain non-medical expenses related to claims. This reduces out-of-pocket costs if chosen.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as... Full list of Non -Medical Expenses is attached as ANNEXURE B... (Annexure B includes items such as) "GLOVES" ... "MASK" ... "NEBULISATION KIT" ...
bad.reference: Section C.3(k) 	6 Specific Exclusions (Page 32) + Annexure B (Pages 49-50)
bad.explanation: Many consumable and non-medical items are excluded by default and must be paid out-of-pocket unless you have opted for Protect Benefit. This can increase your expenses.

bad.name: NCB Absence
bad.quote: Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to Optima Suraksha, Optima Lite and Optima Select plans]
bad.explanation: Some plan variants like Optima Secure do not offer Cumulative Bonus, so your Sum Insured may not increase on claim-free renewals. This limits your coverage growth.

bad.name: Restore Absence
bad.quote: The company shall instantly add 100% of the Base Sum Insured under this benefit... (Automatic Restore Benefit is an optional cover and is applicable... only if it is specified in the Policy Schedule to be in force for that Insured Person...)
bad.reference: Section B.2 	6 Optional Covers intro (Page 14) + Section B.2.6 (Page 17-18)
bad.explanation: If Automatic Restore Benefit is not included in your policy schedule, your Sum Insured will not replenish after a claim. This reduces your available coverage.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Def. 8. Co-Payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.explanation: The policy defines co-pay but does not clearly state if or how much co-pay applies by default. You should check your policy schedule for details.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
